thread.title: Big Apple Stock Buyer: Société Générale Unit

author: Ed Lin
title: Big Apple Stock Buyer: Société Générale Unit
text:
Illustration: Bloomberg News By Ed Lin May 9, 2018 8:00 a.m. ET SG Americas Securities found the apple of its eye in the first quarter.
In fact, the unit of French banking giant Société Générale (ticker: GLE.France) took a major shine to Apple (AAPL), buying 2.5 million shares of the iPhone maker and raising its stake in the company by more than 15-fold to 2.65 million shares, according to data released last week.
SG Americas also saw fit to bulk up in Facebook (FB), Time Warner (TWX), and Avis Budget Group (CAR). The firm, which handles capital markets and investment-banking in the U.S., also doubled its stake in Bank of America (BAC).
SG Americas didn’t respond to a request for comment on the trades.
Apple shares essentially sat out the first quarter, ending March down half a percent from where they started 2018, excluding dividends.
Facebook, for its part, was slapped down 9% in the quarter, as concerns over user-data security and Cambridge Analytica bubbled over into a public-relations disaster for the social network.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg, however, was steady in hearings before Congress in April , restoring a measure of investor confidence. Shares have gained TK% since the end of March through Tuesday’s close, making SG Americas’ purchase look like a prescient buy. It bought 2.8 million additional Facebook shares in the first three months of 2018, ending the quarter with 3 million shares.
SG Americas also made a big bet on Time Warner by purchasing 1.3 million more shares of the media giant in the first quarter, raising its investment to 1.4 million shares. A ruling is expected in June for AT&T ’s (T) battle against regulators to acquire Time Warner. However things turn out, we think Time Warner shareholders will benefit. As Barron’s wrote in March , “Time Warner holders could make 12% in the next few months if the merger closes, and possibly more in a year if it dies.”
Avis had some drive in the first quarter, when the vehicle-rental firm saw shares gain 7% on news that strong demand over Thanksgiving and Christmas lifted December profits. SRS Investment Management, Avis’ largest shareholder, also cheered investors by challenging the company’s management . SRS reached a pact in April to appoint two of its representatives to the board of Avis. SG Americas bought 1.4 million Avis shares in the first quarter, lifting its stake to 1.5 million shares.
SG Americas more than doubled its holdings in Bank of America in the first three months of 2018, a period that saw the bank’s shares inch up nearly 2%. Analysts have been calling for the stocks of large-cap banks to break to the upside for some time now , particularly in the face of tax and regulatory reform . It hasn’t happened yet: Bank of America shares have been flat since the end of the quarter through Tuesday’s close.
SG Americas parent Société Générale is another bank that hasn’t seen much upside this year—in fact, its shares are off nearly 2% so far this year.
